items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Ziroh Labs CEO Says You No Longer Need GPUs to Run AI and He Has the Numbers
items.summary:
While global technology enterprises race to secure multi-billion-dollar GPU clusters, Ziroh Labs is challenging the assumption that AI inference requires dedicated hardware accelerators. Through its Kompact AI platform, the company enables production AI models to run on standard CPU architectures, claiming up to three times the performance of existing CPU-based solutions at 70% to 80% lower operational costs. Founded by Hrishikesh Dewan, whose early career involved building an Assamese-language Linux operating system kernel at IIT Guwahati, Ziroh Labs leverages cryptographic optimization and decentralized computing principles to make AI deployment accessible across resource-constrained environments.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Hrishikesh Dewan, Co-Founder & CEO of Ziroh Labs. They explore the shift from centralized GPU infrastructure to decentralized CPU execution, domain-specific small language model (SLM) architectures, the launch of Kompact AI Box for healthcare and education, collaborating with cryptographer Whitfield Diffie, partnering with IIT Guwahati to launch free LLM foundations coursework, and fostering a research culture that embraces experimentation and failure.

Can CPU-based inference platforms democratize enterprise AI deployment across the Global South?

items.title: EXPOSED: India's 7.8 Percent GDP Growth Is Real on Paper but Fake on the Ground Say Experts
items.summary:
According to MoSPI estimates, India’s real GDP grew 7.8% in Q1, surpassing expectations amidst global economic headwinds. However, this print has ignited a debate over GDP deflator adjustments, base-year revisions, and whether output growth is translating into real wage increases, employment generation, or domestic intellectual property ownership. Prominent economists like Raghuram Rajan questioning job quality alongside tech leaders advocating for domestic IP creation highlight a central question: is India capturing long-term economic value, or functioning primarily as assembly and service backends for global enterprises?

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Jitendra Chouskey (MD & Founder, FITTR) and Prof. Ujjwal Anu Chowdhury (Pro Vice Chancellor, Techno India University). They examine the statistical mechanics behind nominal vs. real GDP calculations, the impact of low agricultural growth and manufacturing double deflation, evaluating PLI industrial policies against domestic R&D, human capital development, and building sovereign IP capabilities.

Does headline GDP growth reflect ground-level economic development and domestic value creation?

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Primebook ARR Hits ₹85 Crore - Startup Builds Indian Android Laptops
items.summary:
While India has successfully established domestic smartphone manufacturing, producing over $38 billion worth of mobile devices, local laptop and tablet production has hovered around $4 billion to $6 billion. In 2018, IIT Delhi graduates Chitranshu Mahant and Aman Verma founded Primebook to address the broken sub-₹30,000 student laptop category. Ditching legacy x86 Intel architectures and heavy Windows OS, Primebook developed an ARM-based MediaTek hardware platform running "PrimeOS", an Android-based operating system designed for low-power, desktop-class multitasking. Today, Primebook generates over ₹130 crore in annual revenue with profitable unit economics.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Chitranshu Mahant, Co-Founder & CEO of Primebook. They explore why legacy OEMs fail to serve budget student demographics, overcoming Chinese supply chain dependencies for display and memory components, software-layer data sovereignty under the DPDP Act, competing against Google’s upcoming Googlebook launch, and expanding PrimeOS across Tier-2/Tier-3 India and global emerging markets.

Can an indigenous, ARM-based Android laptop platform redefine computing access for 250 million Indian students?

items.title: MCP & MCP Runner: The Protocol Behind Agent Communication
items.summary:
Connecting an agent to a new tool used to mean custom integration work every single time. MCP is the standard that removes that.

Terms covered:
- MCP (Model Context Protocol): a standardized way for AI models to communicate with external tools and data sources. One standard, many integrations.
- MCP Runner: the runtime component that manages those connections and makes sure the interactions happen reliably at scale

In practice: a healthcare organization connects an agent to patient records, scheduling and compliance tools through the same protocol. A financial services firm links market data, risk systems and reporting without rebuilding the connection layer each time.

MCP defines how agents talk to the world. The MCP Runner makes those conversations happen.
